title: Graceful entropy buffer and tenant soft-evictor for regional SLO stabilization
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a regional entropy buffer and tenant soft-evictor to reduce oscillatory evictions and stabilize per-tenant SLOs during short traffic spikes. No public API changes.
description:
Context: We observe short, high-amplitude request bursts in certain regions that cause rapid tenant eviction cycles and SLO oscillation. Existing hard-eviction and immediate admission-deny behavior creates noisy signal (tenant churn + KV cache thrash) that increases tail latency for neighboring tenants.

Goal: Smooth admission/eviction decisions over a short time window to reduce churn while preserving responsiveness to sustained overload. Introduce two cooperating pieces: an entropy buffer (small, time-windowed reservoir used by the admission controller to debounce bursts) and a tenant soft-evictor (marks tenants as soft-evicted with TTL and graded penalty instead of immediate hard removal).

What this PR does (single-line summary): Implements a regional, config-driven entropy buffer for admission smoothing and a tenant soft-evictor state machine with progressive penalty decay; wiring includes metrics, flags, unit + integration tests, and a controlled canary rollout.

Design notes: The entropy buffer is a leaky-bucket style token reservoir seeded by instantaneous overload signals (latency percentiles, queue depth, KV pressure). The controller samples the buffer when evaluating admission/fallback decisions; if buffer level > threshold we favor soft-demotion paths (reduced concurrency allowance) rather than immediate hard evict. Soft-evicted tenants receive: a TTLed soft state, a progressive penalty multiplier (0.5 -> 0.2 over the TTL), and a backoff window that prevents immediate re-promote for short bursts.

Config toggles: region.{region}.entropy_buffer.enabled (bool), entropy_buffer.capacity (tokens), entropy_buffer.drain_rate (tokens/s), tenant.soft_eviction.ttl_seconds, tenant.soft_eviction.penalty_decay_seconds, tenant.soft_eviction.max_penalty. Default values chosen conservative for safety; feature flag gated under runtime feature flag 'soft-evictor-2026'.

Metrics and observability added: regional_entropy.buffer_level, regional_entropy.tokens_emitted, tenant_soft_evict.count, tenant_soft_evict.duration_histogram, tenant_soft_evict.penalty_ratio_gauge. Added tracing span 'soft-evict-decision' with decision=soft/hard/allow for topK slow requests. All metrics emitted with region and tenant labels to support drill-down dashboards.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for buffer arithmetic and eviction-state transitions. Integration test using the perf-canary harness that replays synthetic burst traces and asserts stabilization of 95p latency within 3 windows. Canary rollout plan: enable in a single low-risk region (us-west-2) behind a runtime flag for 48h, monitor buffer-level / tenant re-promote rates and SLO regressions. Rollback path: runtime flag OFF and manual cleanup job to promote any soft-evicted tenants immediately.

Backwards compatibility: No changes to public API. Behavior is gated and conservative by default. No migration required.

Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests with perf harness [x] metrics + dashboards updated [x] docs (internal ops runbook) [x] feature-flag gated [x] rollout + rollback plan documented

Why this is different: Existing soft-eviction work primarily triggers on absolute capacity thresholds and performs eviction immediately. The entropy buffer approach uses short timescale smoothing to avoid reacting to single-window spikes while maintaining quick reaction to sustained pressure. This significantly reduces eviction oscillation observed during real traffic bursts in staging.
